results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run them with.

The three requested cards have no published list together. I'll look at each one's neighbours and the Standard field.

Town Greeter lives in the Golgari self-mill shell. I'll pull that shell's latest list, the Rogue list, and the mill and reanimation cards in Standard.

Three directions are taking shape. I'll compare the Dimir and Golgari shells before choosing, and check the mill and ramp cards they share.

Scrapwork Mutt and Haywire Mite are not legal in Standard, so I'll exclude both. Next I'll check the removal and utility cards that fit a Golgari shell and whether the blue splash lands are legal.

Go for the Throat and Cut Down are not legal here, so I'll avoid them. The Golgari shell has the mill and recursion; Spider-Man needs a blue splash, which the Dimir and Town lands can supply. I'll test a first build against the Golgari Roots mana and check the odds of casting Bringer and Spider-Man.

The first check flags the land count: 18 lands is light for a deck with an 8-drop and a splash. I'll move to 20 lands, trimming one Scavenging Ooze and one Cache Grab, and add a Forest and a Swamp for green and black.

The sideboard entry had a malformed line. I'll resubmit the check with a clean 15-card sideboard aimed at the aggro decks and the artifact and enchantment hate the field runs.

The deck passes the checker. The only warning is the land count, which I'm keeping at 20 on purpose: seven mana creatures (four Llanowar Elves, three Molt Tender) plus Town Greeter and Overlord recovering lands from the mill covers the 8-drop. Submitting it now.

The checker flagged four removal and recursion cards as less-played than alternatives. Each has a job here that the alternatives don't do, so I'll keep them and answer each note.

I built a Golgari reanimation deck with a blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. It's a brew: no published list runs these three cards together, and the Golgari Roots shell supplies the mana and mill. The plan is to ramp and mill with Town Greeter, Llanowar Elves and Molt Tender, then recur Bringer of the Last Gift with Overlord of the Balemurk or Coati Scavenger and cast it for eight. Superior Spider-Man is the four-mana backup: it copies Bringer from the graveyard as a 6/6 flyer without the sacrifice trigger.

I chose this over two other directions. A Dimir Spider-Man deck fits Spider-Man better, but it has no ramp or self-mill, so Bringer would be a stranded eight-drop. A pure Golgari build without Spider-Man has cleaner mana but drops one of the three cards you asked for.

Honest odds: the deck has three Bringers, and a Bringer is in hand by turn 8 about 56% of the time. The full win line is drawn by turn 8 only about 2% of the time, so this is a slow deck that needs to survive the aggro start. I kept 20 lands on purpose with seven mana creatures; the checker suggested more, and I accepted that warning. Scrapwork Mutt and Haywire Mite are not legal in Standard, so I left them out, and Go for the Throat and Cut Down are not legal either.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I submitted a 60-card Simic brew (G/U with a red splash) built around Mightform Harmonizer, with Full Bore and Spell Snare as support. None of the three requested cards appears in a current Standard list, so this is a brew, not a proven deck.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. (A) Simic base with a red splash for Full Bore, borrowing the Simic Ouroboroid list (5.6% of the field, a top-3 finish). (B) Green-red Landfall, borrowing its package, but Landfall is about 1% of the field and Spell Snare would be a one-card blue splash. (C) Izzet, which fits Full Bore and Spell Snare but drops Mightform, the payoff. I chose A because its green base supports Mightform's GG cost and its blue creatures give Spell Snare a home.

**The plan:** Ramp with Llanowar Elves and Gene Pollinator, then on turn 4 warp Mightform Harmonizer for {2}{G}. Cast Full Bore on it (+3/+2, trample, haste), then play a land so its landfall trigger doubles its power to about 14 trample damage. Later, Mightform hard-cast and Quantum Riddler, which also has warp, give the same kind of pressure. Spell Snare answers the opponent's 2-drops.

**Odds and caveats:** On the play by turn 4, the odds are about 53% to have Mightform, 68% to have a red source, and 13% to have all three together, and the win line's cards are all drawn by turn 4 in about 4.5% of games. Red is thin at 6 sources (3 Mountain, 3 Multiversal Passage), which is why the checker warns about Full Bore. I ran Full Bore 3 and Spell Snare 2 because each is situational, and I explained that in the submission.

Appa flashes in to airbend Ascension and Bramble so each recasts for {2}, and Aang and Appa carry the air damage. The win line lands around turn 5, and the deck has 21 lands with 7 mana creatures.

The Mono-Red list (13th at Standard Challenge 32) is a Lesson deck built on these exact cards, and Izzet Aggro (1st) is the strongest red-blue shell. I'll pull the Mono-Red archetype data and the card text of the candidate supporting cards.

Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so it's out. Next I'll check the Izzet and Boros shells, plus the white Lessons that would support a Boros direction.

The Izzet Aggro core is almost entirely red, and Abandon Attachments is hybrid, so a red-based Lesson deck needs little or no blue. Before I pick the list, I'll check the lands and the sideboard candidates.

I have what I need for the plan. Abandon Attachments is hybrid, so a red-only Lesson deck works. Soulstone Sanctuary is colorless, which matters with Razorkin's RR, so I'll run one copy alongside 15 Mountains. Running the check now.

The checker flags 16 lands for a deck with 18 one-drops and several mana sinks, so I'll move to 17 lands. That comes out of one Stadium Headliner, and the spare slot goes to a 16th Mountain.

The checker is happy with the list and its 22-land warning doesn't account for this low curve, so I'll keep 17 lands. Submitting now.

The submission was returned with one card note on Stadium Headliner. Floodpits Drowner is blue, so it can't go in this red deck. I'll keep the Headliner and explain its role.

I submitted a red Lesson-aggro deck built on the Izzet Aggro core, with 17 lands (16 Mountain and Soulstone Sanctuary) and a 15-card sideboard. It's tuned from Izzet Aggro, the top red aggro shell in the results, and I cut Screaming Nemesis because it is banned in Standard. The plan is cheap pressure from Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut and Razorkin Needlehead, with Firebending Lesson and Burst Lightning clearing blockers. Abandon Attachments and Firebending Lesson fill the graveyard so Combustion Technique exiles a big threat for a larger amount. Nova Hellkite closes the game.

The three directions I weighed were a mono-red Lesson deck built on the Mono-Red list (which finished 13th), a red-blue Izzet build, and a Boros build with the white Lessons. I chose the red core because it is almost all Mountains, and Abandon Attachments' hybrid cost is payable with red, so the Lessons fit without a blue splash. The white Lessons have no recent Standard results, so Boros was the weakest option.

The deck's win line is turn 6 by design. Its odds of having every card in the line by then are 2.7% in simulated games. The line includes Combustion Technique, which may not be a reliable finisher on its own. The checker warned about 17 lands, but the curve averages 1.86 and the mana sinks cover the extra land.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
The deck is submitted and accepted. It's a blue-red Elemental brew, not a copy of a published list. No published list runs Ashling, Sunderflock, and Bounce Off together, and it hasn't been tested.

**Plan:** Ashling and the Elemental creatures (Shinestriker, Eddymurk Crab, Ice Flan, Mouth of the Storm) lower Sunderflock's cost from 9 to about 3 mana. Once it lands, its ETB bounces every opposing non-Elemental creature while all of yours stay, leaving a 5/5 flyer. Bounce Off and Into the Flood Maw keep the board clear until then.

**Direction chosen:** I compared three. (A) Blue-red Elementals, which I built, because nearly every creature is an Elemental and so survives Sunderflock. (B) Blue-green Elementals borrowing Bounce Off and Spider-Sense from the Simic Ouroboroid package, which drops Ashling. (C) A Simic Ouroboroid bounce shell with Sunderflock as a 9-mana reset, which would bounce its own Ouroboroid counters and creatures. I chose A because it keeps both requested cards and the Sunderflock payoff.

**Honest odds:** Drawing at least one Sunderflock by turn 7 on the play is 52.6%. Drawing a high-MV Elemental to cut its cost is 78.6%. The full win line (Ashling, Shinestriker, Sunderflock, Bounce Off) is in hand by turn 7 in only about 4% of games.

**Things to know:**
- The checker warns that 17 lands is light for a 60-card deck. I kept 17 because the curve is top-heavy, with 2 Stratosoarer and Ice Flan providing landcycling and Flamebraider and Hydro-Man providing ramp.
- The checker flagged Icewind Elemental for rarity in Standard. I kept it as a flying Elemental that counts toward the Sunderflock discount. I swapped Summon: Shiva for Summit Sentinel to smooth the early curve.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how they've been played before.

The three cards have never appeared together in a published list. Next I'll look at the two black-based shells that use them: Dimir Midrange, which already runs Doomsday Excruciator, and Mono-Black, which runs Archenemy's Charm.

Here is the direction I'm weighing before I search:

- **A. Mono-black Doomsday control.** Doomsday needs six black pips and Archenemy's Charm needs BBB, so every land should be a Swamp. The Mono-Black shell already has ~21 black sources and removal.
- **B. Dimir Midrange package.** Dimir already runs Doomsday, but with about 15 black sources, and the cost is too high for two colours.
- **C. Black reanimator.** Archenemy's Charm can return creatures. But a reanimated Doomsday doesn't trigger its mill, because the trigger requires that it was cast.

I'm going with A. Next I'll search the black pool for removal, card draw and bodies.

The black pool has enough removal, a Demon tutor and finishers to build around. Next I'll pull exact text and Standard legality for the candidates.

Two of the candidates matter for the plan. Demonic Counsel tutors any Demon, and Doomsday Excruciator is a Demon. Aclazotz is a modal double-faced card, so its Temple side counts as a land. Next I'll check sideboard options against the field.

The field tells me what the sideboard needs to answer. The leading decks are Simic Ouroboroid, Landfall and Lessons, which bring big creatures, go-wide creatures and enchantments. Next I'll run the draft through the checker against the Mono-Black shell whose mana I'm borrowing.

The list passes the checker with no errors or warnings. It sits slightly under the Mono-Black norm for lands, so I'll swap Fell for a Swamp, which brings the count in line with that shell's 24.1 average. I'll also confirm the basic Swamp's card data.

The checker passes with no errors or warnings, and the land count (24.5 effective) now matches the Mono-Black norm. Submitting the deck.

The checker wants six or more enablers for Doomsday. Insatiable Avarice's search mode can also find it, so I'll count Avarice as a second tutor and resubmit.

I built a mono-black Doomsday control deck around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm, and it was accepted with no warnings. The three cards have never appeared together in a published list, so this is a brew. I borrowed the Mono-Black shell for its mana, removal and black bodies.

The plan: Demonic Counsel (or Avarice's search mode) finds Doomsday Excruciator. Hardcasting it mills both libraries down to six cards. Then two Insatiable Avarice casts, each drawing the opponent three and making them lose three, deck them around turn 8, with Excruciator's 6 flying damage adding pressure. Archenemy's Charm can return a dead Excruciator to hand. The honest caveat is that this is slow: the same mill also shrinks your own library, and the odds of finding Doomsday or Counsel by turn 6 are about 50% each.

I picked this direction over a Dimir build, because Doomsday's six black pips and Charm's BBB need near-mono-black mana, and over a reanimator build, because a reanimated Doomsday doesn't mill.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how they're played elsewhere.

The three cards point toward a discard-and-recursion plan: Iron-Shield Elf's discard cost can put Flamewake Phoenix into the graveyard, and Bloodthorn Flail can make the Elf a 5-power creature for ferocious. Next I'll look for the supporting cards in black and red.

Iron-Shield Elf plus Bloodthorn Flail gives a 5-power creature, which is the ferocious enabler. Next I'll check the power-4+ creatures and red burn that could fill out the deck.

Three directions were on the table:

1. **B/R discard-and-recur (chosen):** Elf, Flail and Phoenix at the center. Elf and Flail give Phoenix a discard route to the graveyard and a power-4+ enabler, and Bitter Triumph and Monument to Endurance feed the discard theme. Red burn comes from the Izzet and Boros packages.
2. **Dimir midrange:** the Dimir package is good, but it would have to cut Phoenix, which is one of the three requested cards.
3. **Boros aggro:** Hired Claw and Emberheart Challenger are strong, but the deck has no way to run Elf and Flail, which are black.

Next I'll check the last two candidates I plan to use.

The checker flags 17 lands against its generic benchmark of about 24. For this 60-card deck with a 2.58 average mana value, I'll keep 17 lands. Discard costs on Elf, Flail, Bitter Triumph and Ultimate Green Goblin turn spare lands into fuel, so the extra land is not dead. Next I'll check how reliably the Elf and Flail combo shows up early.

The deck is legal and the checker's only flags are about land count and color sources, which I've reasoned through above. Submitting it now.

I built a black-red discard-and-recursion deck around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix, and it was accepted. No existing list runs these three together, so this is a brew, and the odds of the full line working by turn 5 are only about 14.5%. The plan: Elf carries Flail to 5 power, Elf discards a spare Phoenix to the graveyard, and from then on Phoenix returns for R each turn with haste and flying. Ultimate Green Goblin, Scavenger Regent, Thornplate Intimidator and Bonehoard Dracosaur provide the other power-4+ bodies, so the engine doesn't depend on the Elf surviving. Bitter Triumph, Monument to Endurance and the discard-cost cards turn excess cards into value, and cheap burn plus Murder handles blockers.

I chose this direction over a Dimir build, which would have had to cut Phoenix, and over a Boros build, which can't run the black cards. I borrowed Bitter Triumph and Monument from the Dimir and Lessons lists, and the burn from Izzet and Boros.

Two things to watch. The deck runs 17 lands, and the checker flagged that as light against its benchmark of about 24. I kept 17 because the curve is low and spare lands are discard fodder. The red count of 8 sources for a RR Phoenix is also thin.

The three cards point in different directions: Rogue runs Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation, and Jeskai Control runs Revelation and Lute. Let me pull both shells.

The main directions are: Jeskai Control (Revelation and Lute are both in its proven list, with Inevitable Defeat needing a black splash), Rogue (runs Defeat and Revelation but not Lute), and a Lute-led instant-sorcery deck (which would lose Revelation's and Defeat's colors). My list was 2 lands short: I dropped the Islands when I made the swap. I'll restore them to reach 25 lands and 60 cards, then recheck.

The deck now passes with no errors and no warnings beyond the white-source note, which the Passages cover. Submitting it as a tuned Jeskai Control list.

I submitted a tuned Jeskai Control list with a black splash for Inevitable Defeat. The plan is to hold up cheap interaction (Get Lost, Lightning Helix, the counters) and use Resonating Lute on turn 4 to double land mana for instants. That mana makes Jeskai Revelation castable on turn 5, and Inevitable Defeat finishes the game later.

I weighed three directions. Jeskai Control already runs Revelation and Lute, so it was the base. Rogue runs Defeat and Revelation but no Lute, and a Lute-led instant deck would lose Revelation's and Defeat's colours. Jeskai was the strongest because the splash is one card, and the other two cards are already in its colours.

The one 4-drop Thorin and the Lonely Mountain give it a mana sink. The 10 red sources against 7 white is intentional, because Mauler and Freya need red on turn 1. Submitting now.

**Plan:** Turn 1 Dwarven Mauler, turn 2 Kíli, then Dwarves and Equipment keep entering so Kíli draws a card each turn. Equipment is then attached cheaply, with Mauler and Kíli both cutting equip costs. Burn clears blockers and finishes the game.

The plan: Thraben Inspector and Spirit Mascot on turns 1–3, then Battle Screech on turn 4 for two Birds and a flashback by tapping three white creatures. Exiling Screech from the graveyard grows Mascot, and Skyknight Legionnaire or Chain Lightning finish the game.

Three things to know:
- **Odds are modest.** Battle Screech is in hand or drawn by turn 4 on the play about 53% of the time. The full line, with every card drawn by turn 5, happens in only about 2% of games, because the deck has 16 multicolored cards and nothing searches for them.
- **Thin gold pool.** Lightning Helix, Boros Charm and Azorius Charm are not legal in Pauper, so Eidolon recursion depends on Mascot, Boros Recruit, Skyknight, Dog Walker and Pursue the Past.
- **Mana.** It runs 19 lands, four of them Boros Garrison, with 12 white sources. The checker flagged the white count against the 16 that Boros Aggro lists run; I accepted it because the red burn needs red sources too.

winLine.does: Turn 1-2 white creature; a body to tap for Battle Screech's flashback cost.
Turn 2-3 white creature; grows +1/+1 each time cards leave my graveyard, and its cast returns an Eidolon from the graveyard if one is there.
Turn 4: cast for two 1/1 flying Birds, then flashback by tapping three white creatures (two Birds plus Inspector or Mascot). Exiling Screech from the graveyard grows Spirit Mascot.
Multicolored 3-drop with flying and haste; adds a hasty flyer and returns an Eidolon from the graveyard to hand.
Burns the last points of damage (3) to face or a blocker while the flyers attack.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I built a black-green Living Death reanimator and submitted it as a brew. It borrows the black core of the Premodern Reanimator list, with green fixing and creatures that Living Death can profitably return.

**Plan:** Buried Alive or Survival of the Fittest fills the graveyard with creatures, Living Death exiles them and sacrifices the battlefield, then returns them all at once. Visara the Dreadful is the main payoff: it comes back as a 5/5 flyer that taps to destroy a creature each turn, and Phyrexian Gargantua and Nekrataal add extra value on their entry triggers. Reanimate, Animate Dead and Victimize give backup reanimation.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. Black-green Living Death with Buried Alive as the mill (chosen). Mono-black with Visara and Gargantua, which is more consistent but has less mana fixing and fewer green payoffs. Hermit Druid milling plus Living Death, which borrows the Hermit Druid combo shell but mills slowly because each activation costs G. I chose the first because Buried Alive and the reanimation spells fill the graveyard and bring creatures back most reliably.

**Odds and caveats:**
- Buried Alive and Living Death are both in hand by turn 5 in about 25% of games.
- The full win line completes by turn 5 in about 7% of games, and that figure does not simulate tutors.
- The deck runs 16 lands plus nine mana sources (four Dark Ritual, four Birds, one Llanowar Elves). The checker flagged the land count as low; I kept 16 because Reanimator lists run about 14 and the extra accelerants cover the gap.
- I left Akroma out because it costs eight mana with WWW, which doesn't fit a black-green deck.
- Living Death also returns the opponent's graveyard creatures and sacrifices my own board, so it works best when I have little on the battlefield.

On turn 4-5, exiles the graveyard creatures, sacrifices our battlefield (Birds and other small creatures), then returns the exiled creatures; Gargantua draws 2 and Nekrataal kills their best nonblack creature on entering.
